newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Kingstream shareholders OK An Feng merger.
newsitem.headline: Kingstream shareholders OK An Feng merger.

text.p: Australia's Kingstream Resources NL said on Wednesday its shareholders voted overwhelmingly in favour of the group's proposed merger with An Feng Steel Co Ltd of Taiwan.
The strong support for the merger is a further boost for the companies' A$1.4 billion steelmaking pro in Western Australia, known as the Mid West Iron and Steel project, Kingstream said.

Under the merger terms Kingstream will acquire up to 100 percent of An Feng in exchange for 615 million shares in Kingstream for A$1.30 each. Kingstream shareholders would own 19.7 percent of the merged group.
After formalities the merger is expected to be completed on July 11, 1997. The merged group will be called An Feng Kingstream Steel Ltd, Kingstream said.

Rowan Johnston, director and joint head of Equity Capital Markets for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, financial advisers to the merger, said that the next stage will be to secure the financing for the Mid-West Iron and Steel Project.

"An Feng Kingstream Steel is expected to contribute about 30 percent of project value through an equity raising in the order of A$650 million, depending on final project costings, with the remainder in the form of debt finance," Johnston said.

"The exact amount of debt and equity required will depend on final project costings. We expect this to be settled in time to enable all the equity to be in place when construction commences in the fourth quarter," Johnston said in a statement.
The Mid-West Iron and Steel project will use iron ore from Kingstream's tenements in Western Australia to produce steel slab in a facility near Geraldton, Western Australia.
The plant is expected to produce 2.4 million tonnes a year of steel slab for export to An Feng's rolling mills in Taiwan. Kingstream shares closed five cents up at 98 cents on Wednesday.
